comparison: Both evaluations agree on the main conclusion (C6, C54, C55) that MCU is a pore-forming subunit of the mitochondrial Ca2+ uniporter. OpenEval finds the combined evidence from three independent lines strongly supports this conclusion, while peer reviewers explicitly state the manuscript 'provides sufficient evidence' and describe it as 'strong evidence.'

Both evaluations support the MCU knockdown experiments (C3, C32-C34, C36-C37). OpenEval emphasizes the statistical significance, specificity controls, and validation at protein/transcript levels. Peer reviewers accept these findings without critique, stating the work 'provides strong evidence' and is 'well written with sufficient evidence.'

Both evaluations support the overexpression experiments (C4, C38, C51). OpenEval highlights the bidirectional evidence (knockdown reduces, overexpression increases) as key for identifying a pore-forming subunit. Peer reviewers accept this data without concerns, stating it 'provides sufficient evidence' for MCU as pore-forming subunit.

Both evaluations strongly support the S259A mutant structure-function experiments (C5, C39, C41-C42, C52-C53). OpenEval describes these as 'elegant' experiments showing dissociation between conductance and drug sensitivity. Peer reviewers affirm this as 'the first structure-function study of the MCU using patch-clamp' and central to establishing MCU as the pore.

Both evaluations support the dominant-negative evidence for oligomeric assembly (C43-C44, C46). OpenEval finds the data consistent with heteromeric complex formation. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the 'strong evidence' for MCU forming the pore, though they group it with the broader mutant analysis rather than evaluating it separately.

Both evaluations support the methodological rationale for voltage-clamp over Ca2+ imaging (C15-C19). OpenEval finds the biophysical reasoning 'sound' about controlling variables. Peer reviewers emphasize this 'methodologically sets an important precedent in the field' and represents the first structure-function study using patch-clamp.

Both evaluations support the whole-mitoplast recording methodology (C47-C49). OpenEval emphasizes the advantages over single-channel recordings in avoiding false positives. Peer reviewers highlight this as 'the first structure-function study of the MCU using the patch-clamp technique' that 'sets an important precedent.'

Divergent evaluations on the I/V curve data (C30-C31). OpenEval supports the experiments as 'well-controlled' with 'appropriate validation' and replicating known IMiCa features. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, requesting clarification about how traces were obtained and whether calling them I/V curves might be 'somewhat misleading' if from ramp protocols.

Both evaluations support the MCU knockdown validation at protein and transcript levels (C25-C27). OpenEval emphasizes the dual validation (Western blot and transcript quantification showing 17±5% remaining). Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the 'strong evidence' without specific critique.

Both evaluations support the oligomeric assembly evidence (C45). OpenEval cites this as consistent with prior work (Baughman et al. 2011) on oligomeric channels. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the overall 'sufficient evidence' for MCU as pore-forming subunit.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake importance (C1, C7-C10) as supported by well-cited prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers focused on experimental findings rather than background literature review.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about uniporter characterization and candidate gene identification (C2, C11-C14) as appropriately cited established work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not separately assess background literature claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims about MCU structure and critique of prior reconstitution attempts (C20-C24) as supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not separately assess this methodological critique of prior work.

OpenEval evaluates the membrane capacitance normalization principle (C35) as supported based on established biophysical principles. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not separately assess this technical detail.
